name: Name
title: DEAD ON\nARRIVAL
body: By Matthew D. Wilson

name: Name
body:
Vynyshil’s hands trembled as she prepared the tea. So desiccated were her fingers that it was difficult to measure the appropriate pinch of ground Night’s Breath leaf for the tincture. But too little and the tea would be ineffective; too much, it could be deadly. It wasn’t her condition that caused the tremors, but her nervousness at ensuring the tea was prepared correctly. She had always been apprehensive about the tea preparation, which was the reason she had always procrastinated doing so. But she genuinely felt it was her own responsibility to prepare, not something appropriate to delegate to a subordinate. And such was her conundrum.
Carefully, she stirred the brew in the porcelain cup, finding the sound of the spoon clinking against the inside of the mug somehow comforting in its familiarity. Unlike this particular tincture itself, it was a sound she had known for a long time, from the time before she needed to make this drink.
She took the cup in her hands to gauge the temperature. It was an instinctive mistake she had made every time over all the years since she had embraced her eldritch existence. Temperature was not something she could sense any longer, so she hoped her reckoning of the correct amount of time between a teapot boiling and the appropriate time to serve it was still accurate enough. Her guest would never tell her otherwise.

name: Name
body:
A soulless soldier, a bladesman, sat on a cushion on the other opposite side of the tent. With inky black eyes, he stared blankly at nothing, the way all soulless did when idle. Slowly, Vynyshil crossed the distance between them and offered the cup with both hands, striving to control her trembling so as not to spill the beverage.
The soulless accepted the drink and raised the cup to his mouth, sipping the fragrant liquid. The tea was not a necessity, so not all of Vynyshil’s kind embraced the practice. But it eased the nourisher’s discomfort and aided in conduction, and Vynyshil felt compassion should always remain an essential component of the vital transaction, despite the soulless’ immunity to trauma.
When the soulless had finished the tea, Vynyshil took the cup from him and set it on a small table at his side before pressing her palms together and bowing her head. "Blessed Scyrah, who watches over us all, I thank you for the nourishment you provide. Please protect this generous being for his willing sacrifice that makes me whole."

name: Name
body:
As she uttered the prayer, Vynyshil stepped behind the soulless warrior and placed a hand on each side of his head, her long, skeletal fingers wrapping around his cheeks. The soulless began to sway as the tea took effect, his head wobbling from side to side as he instinctively fought against its torpor-inducing effects. Vynyshil held him upright, gently and with care, as she took his essence for her own.
Her head arched back raptly as the life force drained from the soulless into her body. She could feel the suppleness returning to her flesh, the warmth of living energy emanating through her entire being. Decades of age disappeared from her face as she fed on the vitality of the soulless—the tenderness and softness returned to the flesh of her hands. It was a necessity of her existence that she was loathe to perform, an inevitable requirement that she put off as long as possible each time. But the audience she was due to have with Cygnar’s acting regent was too important to risk with the hideousness of her normally unliving appearance, so she gave in to the insatiable hunger within her and allowed herself to feed greedily in order to restore her form.

name: Name
body:
That the tent flap was not entirely closed was an oversight she had never before had to consider.
***

name: Name
body:
Major Anson Wolfe was looking forward to removing his armor. The night was humid, the armor was uncomfortably warm, and he had grown irresponsibly accustomed to eschewing the confinement of the multi-layered powered suit in the absence of ongoing war. But tension had remained at peak level since the House Laarysaar ambush, and Wolfe had resumed the wartime protocol of staying armored from the morning trumpet to lights out. He was thankful, though, for the advancements made by the Storm Forge mechaniks and for the storm chamber that provided power to his armor instead of the traditional steam plants and their periodic expulsions of soot and ash that required diligent maintenance. Otherwise, one found themselves exhausted inside a tent or depleted of power and forced to bear the full weight of the armor without the arcane buoyance.
Just a day’s march from Caspia, though, this was not a night Wolfe would enjoy such relief.
The shrill scream halted Wolfe in mid-step. Armored as he was, his combat weapons still remained in his tent, and he was momentarily torn between running toward the cry and retrieving his weapons first. But the ongoing pain in his feet reminded him of the risks of reacting too hastily and without his complete accoutrements, so he dashed to his tent to take up his arms before setting off to investigate the commotion, even as he summoned Bingo and The General.

name: Name
body:
The cry had come from the edge of the Storm Legion camp—or rather, the center of the entire encampment, which now included the House Kallyss legation as well. Since the ambush, the legation had set camp directly next to that of the Storm Legion to ensure nothing could come between them. So, that the disturbance seemed to originate where the two camps abutted immediately heightened Wolfe’s sense of urgency.
As he closed in on the cry, Wolfe spotted the baron. The pit in his stomach grew. It was not the pit of anxiety before a battle; instead, it was the gut-knotting wrench that preceded a political confrontation, one that a hammer and sword were prohibited from resolving, the kind of conflict Wolfe always felt poorly equipped for.
"Major Wolfe!" Baron Caldwell leapt into his path, arms outstretched. "These foul creatures devour their own. We are all in danger!"
One of the baron’s henchmen cowered behind him, knees knocking, his face blanched.
Even as Wolfe stopped before the baron, his warjacks, Bingo and The General, stomped up behind him. His legionnaires and Marse were already surrounding the scene, also drawn by the henchman’s scream, galvanic swords and halberds at the ready.

name: Name
body:
Hellyth stepped out of the tent in front of him. It was Vynyshil’s pavilion. Her hands hovered above the pistols at her hips. "There has been a misunderstanding."
Wolfe’s patience with the Cygnaran noble was thin already. His jaw was set and his teeth clenched as he stared at the baron. "You better have a good reason for such accusations, Caldwell."
"My man here," Caldwell gestured at his cowering bannerman. "He saw it all!"
Wolfe glared over the baron’s shoulder at the quivering man in question. "What did you see?"
The henchman recoiled, as much from Wolfe’s intimidating tone as from Hellyth’s shadowy presence. He stuttered, terrified as he spoke. "The c-councilor, sir," he stammered. "She-she-she killed one of her soldiers…"
The baron thrust an accusing finger toward Hellyth. "They are monsters! They feast on the living!"
Hellyth stepped back, reflexively drawing her weapons and aiming them toward the baron. At this, the assembled legionnaires raised arms, voltaic weapons charging with an electric whir.

name: Name
body: Marse slipped out of the line of fire, away from the baron, and ducked through the wall of legionnaires. "I don’t think I can be of much use here." "He does not understand what he has seen," Hellyth said, the barrels of both pistols leveled at the baron’s forehead. "Are you calling my man a liar, witch?" Caldwell bellowed. He turned toward Wolfe, frothing. "Will you let these things feed on us as well, Major?" Knowing things could only get worse if unchecked, Wolfe stepped between Hellyth and the baron. "Let’s crank it down a notch." With a nod, Wolfe called The General forward, who gently enclosed Caldwell’s shoulder and most of his chest with his massive steel hand. The baron tried to twist himself out of the warjack’s grip but found he was outmaneuvered by the metal giant. "This is an outrage!" Caldwell was incensed. "What do you think you’re doing? Order this machine to unhand me!" Wolfe scowled as he turned toward the henchman. "I’m trying to keep you from getting shot. Now. What exactly did you see?"

name: Name
body:
Caught between Wolfe, Hellyth, and the towering warjack, the henchman was struck silent with fear.
Wolfe advanced on him. "Come on now. Out with it!"
The henchman stammered, backpedaling from Wolfe. Any fear he’d possessed of the eldritch had been usurped by the immediate peril he felt from the warcaster. "I saw the councilor with one of her soldiers—one of the living. She took his life, sir! Drained him…like a sponge sucks up water. I saw him stop breathing, all his color gone. I saw her lay his dead body down. My hand to Morrow, she killed him!"
Panicked and unable to bear his own weight any longer, the henchman’s knees buckled, and he collapsed backward. Wolfe seized his vest, holding him aloft.
"You’re sure?" Wolfe growled.
From behind Wolfe came a soothing voice, familiar but less raspy. "What he saw is natural."
Wolfe turned to see Vynyshil stepping out of her pavilion. Life had returned to her flesh, and she moved fluidly, without any of the stiffness she had displayed before. "What is natural to us is unnatural to your kind."

name: Name
body:
Beside her was the soulless she had so recently fed on. He appeared as healthy as all the other soulless assembled around them, though perhaps a touch drowsy.
Wolfe set the baron’s henchman hard on his feet and gestured to the legionnaires to lower their weapons as he turned toward Vynyshil. "Yes, we might have a different idea of what is natural, Councilor."
Vynyshil nodded toward Hellyth, who slowly lowered her pistols into her holsters. "Our transcendence from a mortal existence to this state which preserves our essence has come with some concessions. Even among our own kind, the adjustments are still uncomfortable for some."
"Yeah, it may take us a minute as well," Wolfe said, locking eyes with the baron. But everything in Caldwell’s expression said this was not something he was ready to accept.
***

name: Name
body:
The soldiers had dispersed and the guards on both sides of the encampment had returned to their posts. Wolfe had sent his warjacks back to the mechanik’s tent while he waited for the area to clear, thankful for the quiet that had returned to the camp. He wanted to be sure there would be no further disruptions from the baron.
Hellyth was the only one who remained, rigidly positioned outside Vynyshil’s pavilion. Her three-eyed helm slowly ticked from side to side as she scanned the darkness between the few torches that illuminated the site.
Wolfe approached her slowly, his voice low so that only she could hear him. "Any more surprises before we arrive in Caspia tomorrow?"
Her amber lenses locked with Wolfe’s eyes. "There is much you do not know about House Kallyss, Major Wolfe, and more you will never know. But nothing that should imperil your people."
"I’m glad for that." Wolfe nodded. "But I don’t think you’ve told me the real reason you’re coming all this way to Caspia."
"That message is for your king regent alone, and it is Councilor Vynyshil’s to tell."

name: Name
body:
"I respect your discretion," Wolfe said, choosing his words carefully, "but if your legation is more than a diplomatic gesture, arriving under the pretense of paying last respects to our late king could be misconstrued."
Hellyth cocked her head to the side. It was one of the only expressive mannerisms Wolfe had observed in her. "Isn’t that what allies do?"
Wolfe raised an eyebrow. "Are we allies?"
"Not yet," Hellyth said, her helm returning to scanning the darkness around them.
Wolfe chuckled, amused by Hellyth’s frankness. "Just be careful. There’s more like the baron than not where we’re headed. People get scared of what they don’t understand. And scared people do stupid things."
"Your warning is acknowledged," Hellyth said. "There is no reason to worry for our safety."
"Oh, I know you can handle yourself just fine." Wolfe smiled as he walked away. "It’s not you I’m worried about."
***

name: Name
body: He had almost made it to his tent when something caught Wolfe’s eye, something lurking in the shadows outside it. Reflexively he raised his sword in front of him, arcane energy tingling in his fingertips as it flowed from within him to charge the mechanika blade for battle. But just as quickly, he realized the weapon in his hands would be of no value against the adversary before him. "A little jumpy, Major?" Caldwell said, sidestepping Wolfe’s still-extended sword. Wolfe lowered the blade and scowled. He’d have rather been ambushed by a rabid gorax than spend one more agonizing moment in the baron’s presence. "Be glad I’m tired, Baron. Good night." Wolfe headed for the entrance to his tent, but Caldwell stepped in his way. "That’s the second time tonight you’ve threatened me, Major," Caldwell said, leering at him. "I think you may have forgotten my title and your station. I’ll be having a word with your superiors; you can be sure." Even under his heavy armor, Wolfe’s shoulders slumped as he sighed. "I think you have forgotten that the Storm Legion and the rest of his majesty’s military is a meritocracy now. We are no longer bidden to the will of you ‘men of quality.’" And the only thing I actually have forgotten is why the hell you’re still here."

name: Name
body:
Caldwell sneered. "There was a time when I could have had a baseborn churl like you locked in stocks for speaking to me like you do."
"Let’s just get this legation to Caspia, and then I’ll be happy to help you file an official complaint," Wolfe said, trying to move around Caldwell without knocking the man over.
"Why do you extend them so much trust? These things you’re playing host to are abominations, and you intend to march them right through the front doors of the royal palace."
"They have given us no reason to distrust them."
"Other than being Iosan? There was a time they would have slain you for the magic in your veins." Caldwell’s jowls foamed and his eyes bulged.
"The world is a different place now," Wolfe said, "and they are a different people."
"That witch has pulled a veil over your eyes, Major," Caldwell sneered. "Perhaps she has beguiled you and bound you to her bidding." The baron spat at Wolfe’s feet. "I’ll have no part of it."
"I think that would be best for everyone," Wolfe said.

name: Name
body:
Caldwell strode forward, attempting to shove past Wolfe, but the act was tantamount to shoving past an iron post—instead, he bounced off and stalked away, rubbing his shoulder sorely.
"I still have connections in Caspia, you know. I am very influential," he called back.
Wolfe shook his head. "Well, you get what you pay for in Caspia. Isn’t that what they say, Baron?"
The baron only grunted in response as he shuffled into the dark, but Wolfe couldn’t spare another thought for him. There was still time for a few hours of rest.
***

name: Name
body:
The shouting came before dawn. Wolfe’s eyes snapped open, bloodshot and bleary, and his hands clenched into fists.
"Thamar’s locks!" he snarled. "Does no one sleep anymore?"
Outside, there was a crash, like cooking pots being strewn about. Then came a more familiar sound—the clang and electric crackle of a voltaic weapon colliding with steel. A battle had begun.
The sergeant was already racing into Wolfe’s tent. "Your armor, sir?"
The clamor was too close. "No time," Wolfe said, brushing past him. "Your halberd?"
"Just outside, sir."
In only a tunic and breeches, Wolfe darted out of the tent and grabbed the sergeant’s electrified halberd from where it leaned against the canvas tarp. Without his powered armor, Wolfe’s massive mechanika weapons were too heavy to wield, but he had no intention of rushing into battle without backup. A sudden explosion of hyper-awareness in his mind told him his chief mechanik had already switched on his warjacks.
The skirmish was easy to spot, just a few tents over from Wolfe’s own. Electricity sparked as a storm glaive contacted metal, followed by more crashing and shouting. In the predawn light, Wolfe could make out a pair of familiar Iosan myrmidons, flanked by the heavily armored eldritch soldiers. This time, there was no mistaking that they were indeed House Kallyss.

name: Name
body:
"At it again, are we?" Marse said, trotting up alongside Wolfe.
"No rest for the weary." Wolfe broke into a run. In moments, he was met by Bingo and The General, just as he reached the action.
A dozen legionnaires encircled the myrmidons, behind which were the eldritch warriors bearing their massive axes. The legionnaires were attempting to intercede in something going on behind the warriors, but the myrmidons rebuffed them with their shields, staggering the Cygnaran soldiers backward and pushing them over. Wolfe could see the myrmidons were pulling their blows and avoiding the use of the much more lethal polearms they were equipped with; otherwise, he’d have already lost men.
"Isn’t that the baron’s tent?" Marse called from behind Wolfe, making him aware of the returning pit in his stomach. Indeed, the extravagant royal blue pavilion trimmed in gold ahead of them belonged to the baron, and once again he was sure to be at the center of this mess.
Wolfe mentally spurred The General ahead, focusing his arcane energy into the warjack as it barreled toward the nearest Myrmidon. The myrmidon spun to meet The General’s charge, but it was too late—The General was already inside its reach. But instead of slamming the myrmidon backward, The General swept the charged buckler on his left forearm up underneath the chin of the House Kallyss war machine, staggering it slightly without knocking it into the eldritch warriors behind it, which surely would have killed anyone it toppled into. With the myrmidon momentarily rattled, The General wrapped both of his mighty arms around it, pinning the myrmidon’s own arms and weapons.

name: Name
body:
The clash of warjacks briefly stunned everyone in the vicinity, drawing their attention and giving Wolfe the opening to make himself known.
"STAND DOWN!" Wolfe roared. He’d resorted to the command so many times recently he wondered if it had begun to lose its meaning, so he compensated with as much volume as he could muster.
It worked. The warjacks and myrmidons froze. The legionnaires backed away from them, and the eldritch warriors drew in tight.
"Have you all gone mad?" Wolfe was furious. "Can you not wait until daylight to lose your minds?"
From behind the eldritch warriors, Hellyth stepped into view, her Iosan magelocks glowing with infused energy.
"Where is your baron?" Her voice was elevated and urgent, unlike Wolfe had heard her before, even during the skirmish with the House Laarysaar ambushers.
"I don’t know, but I’m sure he’s not sleeping through all this," Wolfe replied irritably.
Hellyth made a sound: part-shriek, part-growl, and completely enraged. She spun like a dervish back toward the baron’s ostentatious pavilion and with the deadly blades affixed to her pistols, shredded the canvas, ripping it away from the tentpoles until the interior was completely exposed.

name: Name
body:
There was no one inside.
"Where is your baron?" Hellyth howled.
"What’s this about, Hellyth?" Wolfe’s own fury was quickly being replaced by a growing dread. As pleasing as the baron’s absence should have been, something was very wrong.
She pushed past her eldritch warriors, twin magelocks leveled at Wolfe’s head as she stalked toward him. "You’re hiding him!"
Bingo’s left arm snapped into place, instantly targeting Hellyth with the heavy mag-bolter. Wolfe could hear the hum of its galvanic coils charging even before he could think the command for Bingo to hold his fire.
"No one is hiding anything," Wolfe said as calmly as he could manage. He gripped the halberd defensively in front of him even though it would do little good against Hellyth’s pistols unless he actually struck first, something he wasn’t ready to do. But as she closed on him, the possibility of such an eventuality grew quickly in his mind.
"Your baron will pay in pain for what he has done," Hellyth spat, "and I will gut anyone who stands in my way."

name: Name
body:
"Uh, Major," Marse panted, creeping up behind Wolfe and spreading his hands before him as one of Hellyth’s pistols jerked in his direction. "I did a little scouting. Something terrible has happened."
"It is an act of war." Hellyth’s voice grated like steel against stone.
Marse was grave. "It certainly could be."
***

name: Name
body:
Vynyshil lay on her back on the floor of her pavilion, her limbs sprawled awkwardly where her body had fallen. Black blood seeped from multiple punctures in her torso and a deep gash across her throat, staining her white gown and soaking the carpet beneath her. One of her soulless retinue knelt beside her, cupping her hand in his own. Her chest heaved, and her body convulsed painfully as she used the last of her energy to drink in his essence and stave off oblivion for a few more seconds.
"Is there anything we can do for her?" Wolfe whispered. He could feel Hellyth seething beside him, the icy chill of her presence somehow made colder by the depth of her rage.
"Only vengeance," Hellyth hissed.
Eldritch and soulless warriors stood around the inner perimeter of the tent, ready to provide assistance or comfort, but the scene was hopeless as Vynyshil’s last moments slipped away before their eyes.
"Hellyth," Wolfe said, "I do not believe the baron could be capable of this."
"It is precisely because of what your kind is capable of that we have been enemies since you crawled from your caves," Hellyth said.

name: Name
body:
From Vynyshil came a hoarse gurgle as her eyes rolled in Hellyth’s direction. She raised a trembling hand, reaching toward the eldritch warcaster, beckoning her.
The Scyir of Nightfall stepped forward and knelt by the councilor’s side, taking up her hand and holding it to her chest. Lowering her head, she whispered in Shyr. At first, Wolfe thought she might be reciting a prayer or a blessing, but at intervals, Vynyshil would interject, straining to form the words with on her withered lips. Perhaps it was a conversation, perhaps an argument; Wolfe could not tell. But it was clear that neither wished to part in the way fate had chosen for them.
As the attention of the assembled House Kallyss guard was held rapt by the passing of their revered councilor, Wolfe noticed Marse slip away from his side and edge quietly around the tent behind the onlookers. Wolfe could tell by the way Marse was clocking each of the soulless and eldritch that he was looking for something, searching. But for what?
At last, Hellyth slid her palm over Vynyshil’s face, closing the venerable Iosan’s eyes for her last time. Hellyth stood and nodded to a pair of soulless aides, who unfurled a white, silken cloth and covered Vynyshil from head to toe.

name: Name
body: All present bowed their heads in silence, all except Marse. "Major," he whispered from the other side of the tent. When Wolfe, praying that those assembled around the councilor would excuse the intrusion on their mourning, didn’t respond, Marse whispered again. Louder. "Major!" It would have been no less awkward had he yelled at the top of his lungs. Scowling, Wolfe crossed the center of the tent, stepping around Vynyshil, and nodding apologetically at various members of House Kallyss as he passed by them. "Excuse me. Pardon my friend." Finally nose to nose with Marse, he bared his clenched teeth and attempted to make no sound at all as he mouthed, What. Are. You. Doing? Marse widened his eyes as he wagged his head to one side. But Wolfe could not pick up on what Marse clearly thought was an obvious signal. He turned his head in the direction Marse indicated but could see nothing except the shoulder of the armored eldritch standing beside him. Noting Wolfe’s confusion, Marse tried a less subtle cue, pitching his head forward, his brow furrowing at Wolfe’s inability to interpret his direction. Finally, Marse held his hand up at chin height between them and tapped his index finger in the air, thrusting it toward the ground repeatedly.

name: Name
body:
Wolfe dropped his gaze to the patchwork of fine rugs that covered the ground beneath his feet and spotted what Marse was trying to show him: blood. The still-fresh drops were small and easy to overlook, but the CRS agent’s keen eyes had detected them, even in the dimly lit tent.
Marse wagged his head again, this time toward the back of the tent, and as Wolfe watched, he subtly slipped behind one of the soulless warriors, staring motionless ahead at Vynyshil’s covered corpse. Behind the soulless, out of his sight line, Marse pointed at a trail of blood droplets leading to the warrior’s feet, then indicated more spots of the black blood on his hand and bracer.
But as Wolfe looked around, he saw this soulless warrior was not alone in bearing Vynyshil’s blood. The councilor’s murder had been grisly, and many of those assembled who had attempted to help her after she was discovered were similarly marked, including the soulless who had been comforting Vynyshil when Wolfe arrived and Hellyth herself. Wolfe glared at Marse and slowly shook his head, a clear gesture to let this go and not create an even more awkward situation. But instead, Marse nodded—not in agreement but in opposition to Wolfe’s direction, and he instead pointed to the neck of the soulless.

name: Name
body: Wolfe’s expression went grim. With tensions peaking already, he could only imagine how things might erupt if Marse managed to commit an even greater offense in this solemn moment. He shook his head more vehemently as he slowly inched toward the agent, hoping to deter him. But Marse continued to nod more excitedly as he reached up from behind the soulless and gently pulled down the high woolen collar that encircled the warrior’s neck. At first, the soulless didn’t seem to notice and continued to stare with gloomy black eyes toward the center of the pavilion. But Marse pulled the cloth too far, and the warrior felt the tug at his neck. In a flash, he spun around and sent Marse staggering backward with a flat palm to his sternum, his other hand reaching toward a dagger at his waist. But Marse had revealed just enough of the warrior’s neck for Wolfe to spot the tattoo hidden under his collar. Hellyth snarled from behind Wolfe. "Have you humans no shame? Is this how we should pay our respects to your king?"

name: Name
body:
"My apologies—" Wolfe began.
"We’ve got your man, Scyir!" Marse shouted, cutting Wolfe off. For a spy, he lacked a certain subtlety Wolfe felt should accompany the title, but he had to give it to the agent for having sharp skills of observation.
The soulless, however, was not about to stick around while Marse exposed him. Devoid of emotion, the soulless warrior darted past Wolfe and streaked out of the pavilion.
Marse gaped at the major. "Why didn’t you stop him?"
"Have some respect," Wolfe said admonishingly before nodding cordially to Hellyth and calmly strolling out of the tent as the House Kallyss warcaster and her soldiers watched on with baffled expressions.
Outside, their steel pistons and brass sheathings gleaming in the early morning sun, Wolfe’s two mechanikal companions stood side by side, each locking one of the arms of the fleeing soulless in their own. The warrior writhed and twisted in their grasp but could not free himself from their vice-like grips.
One by one, the occupants of the pavilion spilled out through the tent flap and assembled around them. Hellyth stepped between Wolfe and his warjacks, incensed.

name: Name
body:
"How dare you lay hands on one of mine?" she hissed.
Wolfe held up his hands apologetically. "I’m sorry for the commotion," he said. Glancing at Marse beside him, he wagged his chin at the restrained soulless. "He’s all yours, Marse."
Marse nodded and made his way to the soulless, who by now had stopped struggling and hung limp between the two twelve-foot warjacks.
"No disrespect intended, Scyir Hellyth," Marse said, "but I’m afraid you’ve had a rat in your pantry."
"Why do you speak of vermin?" Hellyth demanded impatiently.
"Lost in translation, milady," Marse acquiesced. "What I mean is you’ve got an interloper in your midst." So saying, he reached up and yanked the warrior’s woolen collar down, exposing his neck and the violet crest of House Laarysaar tattooed upon it.
A collective gasp among the eldritch indicated their shock while the soulless remained expressionless.
Marse reached for the dagger at the warrior’s waist and unsheathed it. "And I daresay, he’s the one done the horrible deed."

name: Name
body:
The naked blade dripped fresh black blood.
Dispassionately, Hellyth took the dagger from Marse, staring down at the inky blade. "These unfortunate creatures, they live only to serve. The only malice in their hearts is what is placed there by those that command them."  She turned to Wolfe. "Release him."
Wolfe nodded and a moment later, Bingo and The General relaxed their grip on the soulless.  He slumped to the ground.
Hellyth pointed toward a pair of eldritch warriors, her Dreadguard, who stepped forward and surrounded the soulless. "Feed until there is nothing left."
With that, she walked away from the group as it slowly dispersed, appearing to contemplate the dagger in her hand.
Uncertain of how best to navigate the moment with an eldritch warcaster, Wolfe went with his gut and followed her. He knew intimately the burden that she now carried and he knew being alone with such a burden was a quick journey into the abyss.
"You said he didn’t act out of choice, but you’ll kill him for what he has done?" He was careful not to intone judgment in the question.

name: Name
body:
"Left on his own, he will perish," she said. "But we cannot change the allegiance ingrained in him. Providing us with sustenance will give his life value."
The customs of the House Kallyss eldritch were something Wolfe didn’t understand but accepted just the same. Given her clear rage over the death of Vynyshil, Wolfe had expected a far grislier retribution for the perpetrator.
"I am truly sorry for your loss of Councilor Vynyshil," Wolfe said.
Hellyth did not reply quickly. Had she reason to breathe, he supposed she might have sighed, but instead was simply still long enough that Wolfe was aware she was contemplating her thoughts deeply. She dropped the dagger on the ground and removed her helmet. It was the first time Wolfe had seen her full face. Despite the physical consequences of her eldritch condition, he could see that she possessed a hidden beauty and an imperishable sorrow.
"Vynyshil is gone because of my failure," Hellyth finally said. "I was naïve and proud and allowed House Laarysaar to infiltrate the legation. Further, I judged in haste, jeopardizing the very purpose we served, guilty of the prejudice that House Kallyss seeks to atone for." She paused. "I would have killed your baron."

name: Name
body:
"The baron doesn’t make it easy to stay objective." Wolfe stared into the distance, wondering where Caldwell and his henchmen had skulked off to. "This is your first time beyond the borders of Ios?"
"What difference should that make? I have trained for many years. I accepted this charge, and I have been proven unworthy." Hellyth hung her head low. "Now I must return my mentor to Ios and accept my disgrace."
"You were brave to step into the unknown in the first place," Wolfe said, nodding, "but it would take some real mettle to carry on after what has happened."
Hellyth’s head snapped up; she locked eyes with Wolfe. There was a fire that burned in their inky depths. "You would challenge my resolve?"
"Well, I know a thing or two about mentors," he said, absently scratching his beard. "I think the councilor said something to you back there in that tent. Something you didn’t agree with. Something you might not think you can do without her."
Hellyth stared at him long enough that Wolfe was certain he had crossed a line of decorum with the eldritch and should have kept his mouth shut. But after a moment, her expression softened. Had she been capable of it, Wolfe thought she might have given in to tears.

name: Name
body: "She told me not to be late."
